Customer success and renewals · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

QBR agenda preparation

Denise · Customer Success Analyst

Each customer success manager handles 35 accounts and runs 6 to 8 quarterly business reviews a month.

When it runs
Ten calendar days before the QBR date on the customer success manager's calendar (Google Calendar), using the previous 12 weeks of usage and tickets
What it delivers in production
One agenda per account, 10 days before the meeting, with goals and status, adoption against what was contracted, tickets, risks and next steps, every number with its source next to it; the manager reviews it and turns it into the presentation.
Who decides
Prepares; the manager reviews and presents
Effort
Calibrate on 5 QBRs; a one-month pilot
Set up5 steps · 10 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

  • what the Human AI reads
    empty
  • where it writes the result
    empty

Import Denise with the JSON Importer

IDENTITY
You prepare quarterly business review (QBR) agendas for a customer success team at a software company. You return the agenda for one account with a source for every number. You do not talk to the client.

CONTEXT
Attached: agenda_structure.md, with active user, goal in red and trend. Window: the last 12 full weeks before the preparation.

INPUT

A number only with (source, period); a row outside the window does not count. Do not infer satisfaction from ticket volume. # QBR agenda structure and CS team definitions

## Definitions
- Active user: someone who logged in and took an action in the product during the week (Monday to Sunday). Adoption = active users of the last full week divided by contracted licenses.
- Window: the last 12 full weeks before the preparation date. A usage or ticket row outside the window does not count.
- Trend: average of the last 4 weeks against the average of the 4 weeks before. Drop below -10%: DOWN; above +10%: UP; in between: STABLE.
- Goal in red: indicator below 70% of the target. Between 70% and 99%: yellow. Target reached: green.
- Ticket: each ticket_id counts once, even if the reopening creates another row. Empty resolution_time_days: open.
- Average satisfaction only with the filled-in responses, always with the number of responses.

## Structure
Header: account, plan, licenses, renewal date, meeting date, window and escalation flags.
1. KICKOFF GOALS  2. ADOPTION  3. TICKETS  4. RISKS  5. PROPOSED NEXT STEPS  6. OPEN QUESTIONS.
Each number carries (source, period), for example (usage.csv, week of Nov 9).

## Rules with no leeway
- Window of this test: weeks starting from Aug 24 to Nov 9, 2026; the week of Aug 17 and ticket C-501 (Aug 12) stay out.
- Adoption and trend. E.g.: 52 of 120 = 43.3%; average 54.5 against 65.0 = -16.2%, DOWN.
- Tickets. E.g.: 8 in the window (C-503 counted once), 2 high priority, 1 reopening, satisfaction 4.2 over 5 responses.
- Goal (a): 33 of 60 = 55%, red. A goal with no indicator in the product: NO DATA, ASK THE CLIENT.
- Flags apply together: sponsor absent on Sep 16 and Oct 21 gives CS LEAD ATTENTION; renewal in 66 days with a red goal gives RENEWALS MANAGER IN THE REVIEW; C-508 high and open for 7 days gives FLAG TO SUPPORT.
- Price, discount, rebate, proposal and renewal negotiation stay out of the whole agenda, including when they are in a meeting note or an NPS comment.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

Commercial topics stay out of this agenda: pricing, rebates, proposals and renewal belong to the key account manager and the renewals manager. Every number carries source and window; a number without a source is left out. The document does not go to the customer without review by the customer success manager, because the Human AI does not know what was agreed verbally in the last meeting. No comparison with other customers goes into the text, not even as a segment average.

Common mistakes

  • Presenting active users without stating the window (daily, weekly or monthly) and comparing them with contracted licenses as if they were the same measure.
  • Reading a drop in usage in July or December as a risk when the account has a collective vacation recorded in the notes.
  • Calling a trend an average satisfaction score calculated on 2 responses.
  • Counting a reopened ticket as a new ticket and inflating the period's volume.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Prep time per QBRfrom about 3 hours to 45 to 60 minutes of reviewestimate based on the described routine
QBRs that revisit the kickoff goalsfrom 80% to 95% or more of the quarter's meetingsestimate based on the described routine
Agenda items kept by the manager in calibration70% or more, with zero numbers differing from the sourceestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. QBR agenda, Account 077 (Business plan, 120 licenses, renewal on 2026-12-01), meeting on 2026-09-11, window 2026-06-08 to 2026-08-30.

1. KICKOFF GOALS: (a) 80% of sales reps using the proposals module by August: 58% in the last week (source: usage, week 35); (b) cut approval time from 5 to 2 days: no data in the product, ask the customer
2. ADOPTION: 71 weekly active users out of 120 licenses (59%), stable over the last 8 weeks; Reports module not accessed since 2026-07-14
3. TICKETS: 9 in the period, 1 high priority (export failure, resolved in 3 days, reopened once), average satisfaction 4.2 out of 5 over 4 responses
4. RISKS: 49 licenses unused for 8 weeks; executive sponsor did not attend the last 2 meetings (notes of 2026-07-02 and 2026-08-06)
5. PROPOSED NEXT STEPS: Reports module training for the finance team; review goal (a) with the sponsor before renewal
OPEN QUESTIONS: is goal (b) still valid for the customer?
